claims.text: AI agents are moving from writing code to operating infrastructure directly, with humans approving changes rather than authoring every one, and this is the central shift in cloud infrastructure in 2027.
Hyperscaler capital spending, Kubernetes-for-AI adoption, and platform engineering are all accelerating in 2027.
Last year's (2026) edition of this Pulumi blog post predicted a cloud-first, AI-driven decade.
Microsoft's Azure business crossed $100 billion in trailing (fiscal-year) revenue.
Google Cloud's backlog reached $514 billion.
AWS's AI business and its custom-silicon (chips) business each passed a $25 billion annualized revenue run rate.
The predictions made in last year's (2026) edition of this post held up.
According to Gartner, by 2028 cloud-native platforms will serve as the foundation for more than 95% of new digital initiatives, up from less than 50% in 2023.
Gartner has forecast that worldwide public cloud spending will exceed $1 trillion in 2027.
Gartner describes cloud as becoming a 'business necessity' by 2028.
According to McKinsey & Company's 'In search of cloud value' report, cloud value driven by innovation is worth 5x more than cost savings.
According to McKinsey & Company's 'In search of cloud value' report, high-performing organizations can achieve an EBITDA uplift of 20–30% by 2030.
According to McKinsey & Company's 'In search of cloud value' report, Asia leads in projected cloud value, followed by the US and Europe.

According to McKinsey & Company's 'In search of cloud value' report, high-ROI organizations excel by aligning cloud strategy with business priorities, building strong cloud foundations, and using modern operating models.
Pulumi Insights + Policies is a unified governance framework that helps teams operationalize cloud value alongside infrastructure as code and automation.
Hyperscalers are making the largest infrastructure investments in cloud history, nearly all centered on AI workloads, inference, and high-performance compute.
AWS posted revenue of $42.2 billion in Q2 2026, up 37% year-over-year.
AWS's Q2 2026 revenue growth of 37% was its fastest revenue growth since 2021.
AWS's revenue growth accelerated to 37% in Q2 2026 from 28% growth in the prior quarter (Q1 2026).
AWS's chips business includes its custom Trainium and Graviton silicon.
AWS's AI business and its chips business are each growing triple-digit percentages year-over-year.
Azure's full fiscal-year 2026 revenue surpassed $100 billion for the first time, reported in Microsoft's fiscal Q4 2026 results (quarter ended June 30, 2026).
Microsoft's fiscal Q4 2026 ended June 30, 2026.
Azure revenue grew 43% year-over-year in Microsoft's fiscal Q4 2026, up from 40% growth in the prior quarter.
Satya Nadella, Microsoft's chairman and CEO, said: 'This year, Azure revenue surpassed $100 billion for the first time.'
Google Cloud revenue rose 82% year-over-year to $24.8 billion in Q2 2026.
Google Cloud's backlog reached $514 billion, up from $106 billion a year earlier.
Alphabet raised its full-year 2026 capital expenditure guidance to $195–205 billion, up from an earlier $180–190 billion estimate that had itself already been raised twice in 2026.
Oracle reported FY2026 cloud revenue of $34.0 billion, up 39% year-over-year.
Oracle's remaining performance obligations reached $638 billion, up 363% year-over-year, driven by large-scale AI infrastructure contracts.
Oracle's AI infrastructure contracts include prepaid and customer-supplied GPU deals now totaling $75 billion.
Hybrid and multi-cloud strategies are now mainstream.
According to ResearchAndMarkets, the hybrid cloud market will grow from $130 billion to $310–330 billion by 2030.
According to Mordor Intelligence, 87% of enterprises run workloads across multiple clouds.
Gartner predicts that 40% of enterprises will adopt hybrid compute architectures in mission-critical workflows by 2028, up from 8%.
In Pulumi's 2026 survey of 510 platform, DevOps, and product engineers, 64% run on AWS, 55% on Google Cloud, and 45% on Azure, with most running more than one cloud.
Pulumi's 2026 State of Agentic Infrastructure survey had 510 respondents who are platform, DevOps, and product engineers.

Pulumi enables consistent multi-cloud provisioning, reusable components/internal platforms, and policy-driven guardrails through its multi-cloud IaC model, Pulumi Policies, and internal developer platform capabilities.
According to Gartner, total worldwide AI spending, spanning software, hardware, and services, is forecast to reach $2.59 trillion in 2026, a 47% increase year-over-year.
IDC predicts that by 2027, half of enterprises will be using AI agents to redefine how humans and machines collaborate.

Pulumi's Superintelligence Infrastructure perspective page explains why AI workloads, from pre-training to inference at massive scale, require dynamic infrastructure orchestration rather than static configuration.
Pulumi ESC manages all secrets and configuration at scale.
Pulumi Insights provides visibility and misconfiguration analysis.
Pulumi Policies provides AI-specific guardrails in code, cost detection, and automated compliance protections.
Pulumi/IaC integrates with third-party data platforms and messaging systems including CockroachDB, Confluent Cloud, and Kafka.
Pulumi Insights Discovery improves cloud resource efficiency and visibility.
Pulumi Policy as Code enforces guardrails, cost controls, and regulatory requirements automatically.
Pulumi Policies incorporates AI-driven optimization and insights that help teams detect misconfigurations, analyze usage patterns, and generate infrastructure updates.
Gartner predicts that by 2028, over 50% of enterprises will use AI security platforms to secure third-party AI service usage and protect custom-built AI applications.
Gartner forecasts total spending on securing AI reaching roughly $4.8 billion in 2027.
Pulumi ESC helps teams centralize and govern credentials, keys, and tokens.
Pulumi offers AI-powered remediation capabilities (linked to Pulumi Insights & Governance product page).

At the Gartner Data & Analytics Summit in Sydney, Carlie Idoine, VP Analyst at Gartner, said: 'AI... doesn't deliver value on its own – AI needs to be tightly aligned with data, analytics, and governance to enable intelligent, adaptive decisions and actions across the organization.'

According to Gartner, by 2026, 80% of large software engineering organizations will establish platform engineering teams as internal providers of reusable services, components, and tools for application delivery.
The 2026 target year of Gartner's platform engineering prediction has now arrived.
CNCF's Q1 2026 Technology Radar report with SlashData found 28% of surveyed organizations already have a dedicated platform engineering team.
CNCF's Q1 2026 Technology Radar report with SlashData found 35% of surveyed organizations are running a hybrid platform that combines existing developer platforms with specialized AI tooling.

Chris Aniszczyk, CTO of CNCF, said: 'Cloud native platforms have reached a point where developers are not just experimenting but standardizing on CNCF projects that make software delivery reliable at scale... What's especially notable about this research is how organizations are extending those same platforms to support AI workloads, showing how cloud native is the base layer of powering the next era of applications.'
Chris Aniszczyk is the CTO of CNCF.
Large tech companies are the first adopters of platform engineering practices, while mid-size to large companies continue to invest in them.
Developer Experience (DX) is sometimes referred to as DE or DevEx.
Gartner predicts that agentic AI deployment in IT operations grows from under 5% in 2025 to 70% by 2029.
Gartner predicts that human-in-the-loop requirements in IT operations workflows fall from 95% in 2025 to 40% by 2028.
In Pulumi's 2026 survey of 510 engineers, 82% agree that AI and agents will meaningfully change how they write infrastructure within 12 months.
In Pulumi's 2026 survey of 510 engineers, 63% say they trust agents to make production changes.
In Pulumi's 2026 survey, manual approval of agent changes remains close to universal today despite stated trust in agents.
Pulumi's report describes the gap between trust in agents and manual approval practice as stated trust outrunning real guardrails.
In Pulumi's 2026 survey, the share of teams expecting agents to generate half or more of their infrastructure code rises from 45% today to 52% within six months.
Pulumi Neo proposes infrastructure changes, runs previews, and executes approved updates with policy guardrails in place.
Pulumi's blog post 'The Agentic Infrastructure Era' argues that AIOps is headed toward a supervised agentic operating model rather than faster dashboards and alerting alone.
AIOps still includes observability, automation, and real-time analytics bridging DevOps, SRE, and IT operations.
According to Mordor Intelligence, the global Kubernetes market is valued at USD 3.13 billion in 2026.
According to Mordor Intelligence, the global Kubernetes market is projected to reach USD 8.41 billion by 2031, a 21.85% CAGR.
The CNCF's Q3 2025 State of Cloud Native Development report puts cloud-native adoption among professional ML/AI developers at 41%.
The CNCF's Q3 2025 State of Cloud Native Development report says 30% of backend developers now use Kubernetes directly, down from a peak of 36% in Q3 2023.
The CNCF's Q3 2025 State of Cloud Native Development report attributes the slow decline in direct Kubernetes use among backend developers to the technology's growing maturity.
Teams still need flexible GPU scheduling, distributed pipelines, and portable execution environments as AI workloads scale.

Pulumi has published a comparison of Kubernetes IaC tools (best-kubernetes-iac-tools-2026) and an article on Kubernetes evolving in response to AI demands (beyond-yaml-kubernetes-2026-automation-era).

Inference workloads powered by LLMs and GPUs now require low-latency execution closer to the user, and organizations often leverage Kubernetes as the common control plane for AI cluster orchestration across edge and core clusters.
Kubernetes is evolving to support AI through GPU-aware scheduling and more advanced workload orchestration.

AI-powered coding assistants like GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, and Cursor have moved from novelty to everyday tooling for a large share of enterprise software teams, and the same shift is now reaching infrastructure code.
According to Gartner, by 2028, 75% of enterprise software engineers will use dedicated AI code assistants.
According to Gartner, 63% of organizations are currently piloting, deploying or beginning to use AI code assistants.
The July 2026 revision of the Model Context Protocol is described by its maintainers as the largest revision of the protocol to date.
AWS shipped a general-availability MCP server for its Agent Toolkit.
Mirantis's Lens has launched a built-in MCP server connecting AI coding assistants to Kubernetes.
The July 2026 revision of the Model Context Protocol is part of what makes direct action by AI assistants on infrastructure practical.
Pulumi released Pulumi Agent Skills, a collection of infrastructure expertise packaged for use in AI coding assistants.
Pulumi Agent Skills teach tools such as Claude Code, Cursor, or Gemini CLI to reason about Pulumi projects, reducing hallucination and improving outputs.
The release of Pulumi Agent Skills is one of the newest developments in AI coding assistant support for Pulumi.
Pulumi has a Remote MCP Server that gives AI assistants infrastructure access, and Pulumi Neo executes actions with previews, policies, and orchestration.
AI code assistants are no longer experimental and are fast becoming a competitive advantage in cloud software development.
Cloud infrastructure is entering its most transformative era since the rise of Kubernetes.
Modern IaC, unified governance, reusable components, and policy frameworks are all core capabilities of the Pulumi Cloud platform.
The gap between teams that modernize and those that do not will widen rapidly in 2027 and beyond.
